newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ wool prices generally ease at Napier sale.
newsitem.headline: NZ wool prices generally ease at Napier sale.

text.p: Wool prices generally eased back at a sale in Napier on Thursday, the market indicator falling six cents to 450 NZ cents per kg clean, Wools of New Zealand said.
The strong segment indicator fell nine cents to 381, while the lamb segment rose one to 415 cents.

Compared to the May 22 sale, prices for crossbred fleeces were up to five percent cheaper. Second shear was up to four percent cheaper, first lambs was fully firm, and second shear bellies and pieces were up to 2.5 percent dearer.

Of the 2,046 clean tonnes on offer, 29 percent was passed in. The offer comprised 20 percent crossbred fleece, 64 percent second shear, 10 percent second shear bellies and pieces and four percent lambswool.
New Zealand exporters said the main bidding came from local mills, Western Europe, China and India and Pakistan.
The next sale is scheduled for Christchurch on June 19.
